title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
layout_note: Two parallel columns between an input bar x at the bottom and an output bar h at the top: a large blue square (pretrained W) on the left and a pair of orange trapezoids (A below, B above, narrowing to rank r between them) on the right, meeting at a plus.
grouping: No containers. Colour separates roles: the frozen pretrained weight is one blue square, the trainable low-rank factors are orange, the input and output vectors are yellow bars.
shapes_depth: Flat, square corners. The trapezoids' shape draws the bottleneck: A narrows from width d to r, B widens back; braces label d under the input and r between the trapezoids. Hollow outlined block arrows lead from x into both columns and from both columns up to a large outlined plus beneath h. Math (W in R^{d x d}, B = 0, A = N(0, sigma^2)) is written inside the shapes.
proposed_highlight: The added low-rank path is drawn in saturated orange beside a single plain blue block for the frozen weights, and its trapezoid shape alone conveys the rank reduction.
lesson: Draw a low-rank factorisation as two trapezoids that pinch to a narrow waist labelled r, beside one large square for the full matrix, so the size contrast says 'small trainable add-on' without text.
notes: elements 'brackets' = the d and r braces. Crop made by hand with PyMuPDF from page 1 (refs crop found no caption because the caption sits beside the figure and is broken across columns); no figN.json, so photo_share is unknown (the figure is vector only). Venue: the arXiv v2 first page prints no venue; remembered as ICLR 2022. year = arXiv preprint year.

arrangement.units: no enclosures: two side-by-side columns (a frozen-weight square and a stacked pair of trapezoids) between an input bar at the bottom and an output bar at the top
arrangement.inputs_as: a yellow bar labelled x with a brace marking its width d
arrangement.shared: the input x feeds both columns through two hollow block arrows, and their outputs meet at one plus glyph below h

core.what: two side-by-side paths from input x, a large blue 'Pretrained Weights' square and an orange bottleneck of two trapezoids A and B, summed at a + into h

relations.form: hollow arrows from the yellow x bar into both the blue square and trapezoid A, and from both the square and trapezoid B into one + above, then into the yellow h bar
bottom to top on the right: A narrows from width d to width r, B widens back, the bottleneck drawn as two facing trapezoids
brackets mark d under x and r at the bottleneck, so the low rank is visible as the narrow waist between A and B

channels.colour: blue = frozen pretrained weights, orange = the added low-rank factors, yellow = activations x and h; one meaning each, unkeyed but obvious
channels.shape: square = full d x d matrix, trapezoid = a rank-changing projection, flat bar = activation vector

quality.strengths: The method is geometry: shape width encodes dimension (d-wide square, trapezoids pinching to r), the new part is the saturated orange pair beside the frozen blue block, and input and output are drawn as bars at the bottom and top with only short straight arrows.
quality.weaknesses: Blocks carry formulas (W in R^{d x d}, A = N(0, sigma^2), B = 0) for initialisation rather than names; the colour roles (frozen vs trained) are not keyed and rely on the caption.

insights.structure: A frozen weight square and a trainable trapezoid pair stand side by side as two parallel paths between one input bar and one output bar.
insights.data: Input and output are flat yellow bars labelled x and h, with their dimension given by a brace (d) rather than a tensor drawing.
insights.emphasis: Saturated orange trapezoids that pinch to a labelled width r set the trainable low-rank path apart from the single blue pretrained block.
insights.flow: Read bottom to top: from x up through both columns along hollow block arrows into the plus and out to h.
insights.avoid: Nothing in the figure marks W as frozen and A, B as trained; that distinction lives only in the caption.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
